# DEFENDER'S OPENING

I am the defender. I open and hold the standard reading of this topic: **Christ had no biological father.** The record states that the child was conceived "of the Holy Ghost" in Mary, a virgin who "knew not a man," before she and Joseph "came together," and that Joseph "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." My method is fixed by the burden rule: I build only on rows that affirm. I require no verse to state a denial, and I rest on no verse's silence.

**The topic in the record's own words.** The record's word for biological fatherhood is "begat": [L1] Matthew 1:2 — "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judas and his brethren;" — [L2] γεννάω (gennaō, G1080, "beget, become the father of"). [L4] On [L1] Matthew 1:2 and [L2] gennaō, together with the father-subject pattern of Matthew 1:2-16 exhibited in LINK 4 below: to have a biological father, in this record's terms, is to be begotten of a man. The question is what the record states about the begetting of Jesus. Five links carry the answer.

## LINK 1 — the record states the source of the child: "of the Holy Ghost"

[L1] Matthew 1:18 — "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

[L2] The verse opens with γένεσις (genesis, G1078, "birth, generation") and οὕτως (houtōs, G3779, "thus, on this wise"): the record announces that it will state the manner of the birth, and the first fact it states is the source — ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου (ek pneumatos hagiou, "of the Holy Ghost"; πνεῦμα, pneuma, "spirit, ghost"; ἅγιος, hagios, "holy"), with ἐκ (ek, G1537, "of, out of," the preposition of source). The child is stated to be "of the Holy Ghost."

[L1] Matthew 1:19 — "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." — the record states the mind Joseph had on this finding.

[L1] Matthew 1:20 — "But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

[L2] The same preposition of source stands again — ἐκ πνεύματός ἐστιν ἁγίου ("is of the Holy Ghost") — and the child is named τὸ ἐν αὐτῇ γεννηθέν (to en autē gennēthen, "that which is conceived in her"), from γεννάω (gennaō, G1080, "beget, conceive"), the same verb the record renders "begat" throughout Matthew 1. The ground-marker γάρ (gar, G1063, "for, because") shows what the stated origin is doing in the record: it is the reason the angel gives why Joseph should "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife."

[L3] Luke 1:35 — "And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." — the same source, named to Mary.

[L4] Inference, on [L1] Matthew 1:18 + [L1] Matthew 1:20 + [L2] ek ("of, out of," source) and gennaō ("beget, conceive") + [L3] Luke 1:35: the record states the origin of the child three times — in the narrator's voice (Matthew 1:18), in the angel of the Lord's word to Joseph (Matthew 1:20), and in the angel Gabriel's word to Mary (Luke 1:35) — and every statement names the Holy Ghost as the source of the conception.
